Reasons To Stay Away From Common Do It Yourself
Wireless Camera Installations

Brands such as Arlo, Ring, Google, Nest, Blink and TP-Link Tapo all offer do-it-yourself security installations, which at first sound very tempting; however, consider the following points which is why you would want to fill in our quote form to get a professional to quote you on a hard-wired security solution.

Reliability

Wired cameras provide a stable and continuous connection, ensuring consistent surveillance without the risk of signal drops or interference that can affect wireless systems.

Security

Wired systems are less vulnerable to hacking than wireless cameras, which transmit data over the air and can be intercepted by tech-savvy intruders.

Video Quality

With wired cameras, you can expect higher resolution and clearer video feeds because they are not limited by bandwidth or signal strength issues common in wireless setups.

No Batteries Required

Unlike some wireless cameras that rely on batteries, wired cameras are connected directly to the power source, eliminating the need for frequent battery replacements and ensuring uninterrupted operation.  Too often, we hear cameras running out of battery when an incident occurs, making your investment worthless if you have to recharge every couple of days.

Long-Term Cost-Effectiveness

Although the initial setup might require more effort and resources, wired cameras are more durable and require less maintenance over time, making them a more cost-effective solution in the long run. A lot of the time, you have to pay for notifications and mobile device access in order to best utilise the cameras, which can add up the cost.

Scalability

Wired systems can be expanded more easily with additional cameras without worrying about bandwidth limitations or additional strain on your Wi-Fi network.

Frequently Asked Questions relating to CCTV Camera's and being installed.

Whats the difference between someone who has a master security License compared to someone who doesnt?

Not only are we licensed and qualified to install security cameras, but we are a master Cabler as well which means your cabling will be neat and tidy and follow industry standards.  You can ensure that the job is done with the expectations a fully experienced Data cable Installer can offer compared to other companies that may just be starting out.  Some common Beginner mistakes we have seen while attending addresses in Stretton include;

  • Poor Camera Placement
  • Neglecting sufficient Lighting
  • Failure to secure cameras properly
  • Cabling is messy and obviously done by someone who’s not qualified
  • Failing to consider privacy concerns
What are the different types of CCTV Cameras?

With so many types of security options to choose from this is a brief overview of the type of camera’s we can work with.

IP Camera or Network Camera, Most cameras are IP only now since there is no use of cameras that you can only access from a particular place.  We are usually upgrading these older systems so that they are IP cameras that allow you to check your security footage and live feed from anywhere in the world.

Turret Camera, Small, rounded cameras you see everywhere. This is commonly used either in residential or commercial areas.  These are dome-shaped cameras pointing to one side that can have a wider capture angle.

Bullet Camera, You might have seen this in many shops and malls. This device has a long head (typically you see them in photos and movies).  These are great for getting very specific areas and zooming up close for getting License Plate numbers.

Dome Camera, As per the name, dome-like. Mostly used in indoor cameras for commercial security as it hides the lens tricking criminals about which side lens is looking unlike the Turret Camera’s above.

Can your CCTV Record sounds?

All of our systems are able to record sound and some also have 2 way Audio where you can speak to the person who has triggered the alarm, example mail delivery services and giving them permission to leave your package somewhere of your choosing.

Can CCTV be used as evidence

CCTV footage is a crucial tool in legal and law enforcement scenarios. It can be utilized extensively for the prevention, detection, investigation, prosecution, or punishment of criminal offences. Additionally, it is valuable in the preparation for or conduct of proceedings before any court or tribunal. The footage must be handled and used correctly to serve as reliable evidence in legal contexts.  It’s important that this copy is clear, unaltered, and includes a timestamp and date. This helps in establishing a precise and uncontested timeline of the events captured.

Will my QLD Insurance policy come down for having CCTV cameras installed?

Out of 36 major insurers in QLD, only 12 offered some form of discount or benefit for having a security system installed one of which is RACQ, which offers a 10% discount if an alarm system is monitored.  However, more important to note is that the majority of insurance companies in QLD take CCTV security cameras into consideration when calculating your premiums but do not specify the discount amount.  You can usually find this out by telling them about what your going to get installed and asked them to give you a new updated premium which would be specific to your need but your area and crime statistics as shown above will also be used in deciding your premiums.

The scary thing is that many insurers have clauses excluding coverage if a security system is not installed, functioning, disconnected, or affected by cyber-attacks or renovations at the time of a break-in or theft. This is not something that you would like to find out about, thinking you’re insured and realising that it was a hidden clause.  No wonder why so many people can despise insurance companies.

To get the most accurate and up-to-date information on discounts and coverage related to CCTV cameras or security systems, it’s recommended to contact the specific insurance providers and review their Product Disclosure Statements or simply give them a call which will be way easier.

Reasons To Stay Away From Common Do It Yourself
Wireless Camera Installations

Brands such as Arlo, Ring, Google, Nest, Blink and TP-Link Tapo all offer do-it-yourself security installations, which at first sound very tempting; however, consider the following points which is why you would want to fill in our quote form to get a professional to quote you on a hard-wired security solution.

Reliability

Wired cameras provide a stable and continuous connection, ensuring consistent surveillance without the risk of signal drops or interference that can affect wireless systems.

Security

Wired systems are less vulnerable to hacking than wireless cameras, which transmit data over the air and can be intercepted by tech-savvy intruders.

Video Quality

With wired cameras, you can expect higher resolution and clearer video feeds because they are not limited by bandwidth or signal strength issues common in wireless setups.

No Batteries Required

Unlike some wireless cameras that rely on batteries, wired cameras are connected directly to the power source, eliminating the need for frequent battery replacements and ensuring uninterrupted operation.  Too often, we hear cameras running out of battery when an incident occurs, making your investment worthless if you have to recharge every couple of days.

Long-Term Cost-Effectiveness

Although the initial setup might require more effort and resources, wired cameras are more durable and require less maintenance over time, making them a more cost-effective solution in the long run. A lot of the time, you have to pay for notifications and mobile device access in order to best utilise the cameras, which can add up the cost.

Scalability

Wired systems can be expanded more easily with additional cameras without worrying about bandwidth limitations or additional strain on your Wi-Fi network.

What are the different types of CCTV Cameras?

With so many types of security options to choose from this is a brief overview of the type of camera’s we can work with.

IP Camera or Network Camera, Most cameras are IP only now since there is no use of cameras that you can only access from a particular place.  We are usually upgrading these older systems so that they are IP cameras that allow you to check your security footage and live feed from anywhere in the world.

Turret Camera, Small, rounded cameras you see everywhere. This is commonly used either in residential or commercial areas.  These are dome-shaped cameras pointing to one side that can have a wider capture angle.

Bullet Camera, You might have seen this in many shops and malls. This device has a long head (typically you see them in photos and movies).  These are great for getting very specific areas and zooming up close for getting License Plate numbers.

Dome Camera, As per the name, dome-like. Mostly used in indoor cameras for commercial security as it hides the lens tricking criminals about which side lens is looking unlike the Turret Camera’s above.

Can your CCTV Record sounds?

All of our systems are able to record sound and some also have 2 way Audio where you can speak to the person who has triggered the alarm, example mail delivery services and giving them permission to leave your package somewhere of your choosing.

Can CCTV be used as evidence

CCTV footage is a crucial tool in legal and law enforcement scenarios. It can be utilized extensively for the prevention, detection, investigation, prosecution, or punishment of criminal offences. Additionally, it is valuable in the preparation for or conduct of proceedings before any court or tribunal. The footage must be handled and used correctly to serve as reliable evidence in legal contexts.  It’s important that this copy is clear, unaltered, and includes a timestamp and date. This helps in establishing a precise and uncontested timeline of the events captured.

Will my QLD Insurance policy come down for having CCTV cameras installed?

Out of 36 major insurers in QLD, only 12 offered some form of discount or benefit for having a security system installed one of which is RACQ, which offers a 10% discount if an alarm system is monitored.  However, more important to note is that the majority of insurance companies in QLD take CCTV security cameras into consideration when calculating your premiums but do not specify the discount amount.  You can usually find this out by telling them about what your going to get installed and asked them to give you a new updated premium which would be specific to your need but your area and crime statistics as shown above will also be used in deciding your premiums.

The scary thing is that many insurers have clauses excluding coverage if a security system is not installed, functioning, disconnected, or affected by cyber-attacks or renovations at the time of a break-in or theft. This is not something that you would like to find out about, thinking you’re insured and realising that it was a hidden clause.  No wonder why so many people can despise insurance companies.

To get the most accurate and up-to-date information on discounts and coverage related to CCTV cameras or security systems, it’s recommended to contact the specific insurance providers and review their Product Disclosure Statements or simply give them a call which will be way easier.
